# dlarmm

> Compute a safe BLAS-style constant for scaling matrix norms.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlarmm from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlarmm';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlarmm( anorm, bnorm, cnorm ) → number
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anorm` | `number` | in |  |  | the infinity norm of A. |
| `bnorm` | `number` | in |  |  | the infinity norm of B. |
| `cnorm` | `number` | in |  |  | the infinity norm of C. |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `anorm`: The infinity norm of A. $\mathrm{ANORM} \ge 0$. The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `bnorm`: The infinity norm of B. $\mathrm{BNORM} \ge 0$.
- `cnorm`: The infinity norm of C. $\mathrm{CNORM} \ge 0$.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: result

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlarmm.ndarray( anorm, bnorm, cnorm ) → number
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anorm` | `number` | in |  |  | the infinity norm of A. |
| `bnorm` | `number` | in |  |  | the infinity norm of B. |
| `cnorm` | `number` | in |  |  | the infinity norm of C. |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `anorm`: The infinity norm of A. $\mathrm{ANORM} \ge 0$. The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `bnorm`: The infinity norm of B. $\mathrm{BNORM} \ge 0$.
- `cnorm`: The infinity norm of C. $\mathrm{CNORM} \ge 0$.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: result

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlarmm()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARMM`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlarmm.f).
-   See LAPACK reference documentation for full algorithmic details.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dlarmm from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlarmm';

// For modest infinity norms, no down-scaling is required:
const s1 = dlarmm( 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 );
console.log( s1 );

// When the product would overflow, dlarmm returns a smaller scaling factor:
const s2 = dlarmm( 1e308, 1.0, 1e307 );
console.log( s2 );

// When `bnorm > 1` and the product would overflow, the factor scales by 1 / bnorm:
const s3 = dlarmm( 1e308, 10.0, 1e307 );
console.log( s3 );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARMM`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLARMM returns a factor s in (0, 1\] such that the linear updates

$$
(s \, C) - A \, (s \, B) \quad\text{and}\quad (s \, C) - (s \, A) \, B
$$

cannot overflow, where A, B, and C are matrices of conforming dimensions.

This is an auxiliary routine so there is no argument checking.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
